short: Word-level ECoG encoder-decoder; all changed components standard. 3% WER is on repeats of 50 sentences; unseen sentences and participants were never tested.
position: Makin et al. [@makin2020] changed the decoder (M06, an autoregressive encoder–decoder), the output unit (M08, words), the training-only targets (M02, MFCC regression) and the training data (M03, transfer); all four are standard. An attention encoder–decoder had already decoded EEG to text [@krishna2019], and Brain2Char [@sun2020] [concurrent] used the same MFCC loss. The internal protocol is strong: 30 models per condition, matched held-out blocks, corrected tests and a length-only noise control. The headline 3% WER comes from held-out repeats of the same 50 sentences, so the claimed gain over the cited 60% baseline [@herff2015], tested leave-one-phrase-out, compares unlike protocols. Unseen sentences and participants were never tested; today's reference is 23.8% WER on never-repeated sentences with 125,000 words [@willett2023].
